name: What is the practical difference between installing marble tile versus porcelain tile?

mainEntity.name: What is the practical difference between installing marble tile versus porcelain tile?

acceptedAnswer.text: Marble is a natural, porous stone, whereas porcelain is manufactured and non-porous. In daily use, marble offers unmatched, one-of-a-kind veining and high luxury appeal, but it requires regular sealing and is vulnerable to acidic etching from spills like wine or vinegar. Porcelain tile reproduces stone patterns effectively, resists stains without sealants, and requires far less ongoing maintenance. Choosing marble means committing to periodic care and specialized stone cleaners to preserve its surface, while porcelain trades genuine organic variation for scratch and stain resistance.
acceptedAnswer.description: Marble offers authentic natural veining but requires regular sealing, whereas porcelain is non-porous, highly stain-resistant, and requires little ongoing maintenance.
